newsitem.title: GERMANY: OPINION - Hypo-Bank on German bond outlook.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Hypo-Bank on German bond outlook.

text.p: By Manfred Lindermayer, head of research at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, Munich.
U.S. BOND MARKET TO HAVE STABILISING INFLUENCE ON INTERNATIONAL BOND MARKETS -- EMU DEBATE IS ACTING AS A BURDEN.

An interest rate move by the Federal Reserve at the next FOMC meeting on July 1 and 2 remains a realistic option. The U.S. jobs market report for May did not provide new clues to the outcome of the meeting. The report gave scope for divergent interpretations because of the strong revision of the previous month's data. But overall, the components show the labour market remains in a firm state.

The labour market is the only area where potential risks of upward wage pressures with negative effects on the inflation rate can be detected. Another tightening would be interpreted by the markets as the Fed's last insurance for the time being against an economic overheating and for sustained price stability. We therefore expect the U.S. bond market to have a stabilising influence on the international bond markets.

The results of the French election are hard to assess in the short-term in particular as regards the working relationship between President Jacques Chirac and the new Prime Minister, Lionel Jospin. But an interim assessment allows the conclusion that the French position in European Union decision-making will not change fundamentally. But it is likely to become apparent that France intends to give precedence to a more generous interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty and the stability pact rather than to exact adherence to the criteria. This suggests there will be a larger group of participants in the EMU start-up phase -- but markets expect this to happen. At the same time Eurosceptics will gain weight in the public debate and delay scenarios will come to the fore.

If one lists the highlights of the the two past weeks it is remarkable how little markets have reacted. Of course the outcome of the French parliamentary elections was not surprising after the results of the first round of voting. In addition the attempts by Bonn to arrive at a joint strategy with the Bundesbank regarding the valuation of gold and currency reserves were to be expected after the conflict escalated rapidly. In addition the budget negotiations between the Bonn coalition parties are sluggish and still controversial, but in the final analysis they reflect the desire to reach a compromise acceptable to both sides.

Looking at all current problems one can however only conclude that the opportunity/risk relationship has worsened for the German bond market. This applies despite the fact that the most recent interim recovery of the market improved what had been a critical technical situation.
MODERATE YIELD RISE ON GERMAN BOND MARKET AND NARROWING SPREAD TO THE U.S.

After the yield low of about 5.50 percent (REX-10) in February we predicted a yield upturn in the German bond market caused by fundamental factors. In the course of the second half of 1997 we expect a shift in the yield range to 6.00 - 6.50 percent and an unchanged year-end level of about 6.40 percent. After the volatilities on the European bond markets (and on the currency markets) markedly declined in recent weeks, we expect nervousness to grow again. More critical assessments of the EMU complex will no longer be reflected in a favouring of the German bond market. In addition the trend towards an underperformance of Bunds against U.S. Treasuries will continue. That is why we expect the 10-year yield spread to narrow to about 50 basis points after widening to up to 115 basis points in previous weeks.

On the money market we expect no change in conditions. The Bundesbank can justifiably point out that it has created the conditions for an economic revival. The increasingly tense political environment should cause the Bundesbank to refrain from even marginal loosening steps. We also see no need for a change in direction in monetary policy until well into 1998.

The opinions expressed in this column represent those of the author only. They should not be seen as representing the views of Reuters. The translation from the German language into English was carried out by Reuters.
